description:
Inflamiotic uses NASA microgravity combustion data and SI-based analysis to study how flames behave in space. We will analyse datasets, develop visualisations, compare combustion patterns, and identify insights to improve spacecraft fire safety.

Looking for team members specialized in data-statistics, experienced and avid astrophysicists, coders, software engineers or just people interested in software in general

Feel free to join this project, whether your qualified or not
summary:
Inflamiotic is an interactive, SI-powered scientific analysis platform designed to investigate combustion behavior in microgravity. Using NASA's microgravity combustion datasets, the platform transforms complex experimental measurements into accessible visualizations, interactive comparisons, and data-driven insights.

It enables users to explore flame behavior, combustion characteristics, and changes in physical phenomena under microgravity conditions. Through scientific data processing, interactive visualizations, and AI-assisted interpretation, Inflamiotic aims to uncover patterns that may be difficult to identify across large experimental datasets.

The project addresses the challenge of understanding fire behavior in spacecraft, where microgravity fundamentally alters combustion processes and creates unique fire-safety concerns. By making NASA's experimental data easier to explore and interpret as well as visualize, Inflamiotic aims to contribute to research supporting safer spacecraft design and future human exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
details:
INFLAMIOTIC

INFLAMIOTIC is a web-based research explorer for NASA combustion and fire-safety experiments. It brings investigation summaries and the NASA data files supplied with the project into one place, so visitors can browse findings, compare fuels and test conditions, and understand what the results may mean for crew safety.

What it does and how it works

The site organizes investigation records into searchable sections, including research rankings, modeling and equipment information, space environments, fuels and flammability, and newly added evidence. Users can filter investigations and open a detail page with experiment context, tested conditions, and a summary of the research’s relevance.

Its data views work from the provided files. Depending on the dataset, visitors can explore measurements through charts such as bar, pie, line, and scatter plots, inspect source records, and download charts as PDFs or Python code for use with Matplotlib. The site mainly includes PSI-10, PSI-159, and PSI-26 data, along with other supplied NASA tables and research files.

The project also contains multiple sections that are further divided into subsections addressing various topics and analysis of different datasets

Benefits and intended impact

The project makes a collection of technical research easier to navigate for students, educators, and people interested in spaceflight safety. It helps users see how conditions such as oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity, fuel, and materials relate to the experiments that were performed.

The intended impact is to support learning and informed discussion about fire safety for future crews, while making the underlying evidence easier to inspect. The site is an educational research tool; it does not replace NASA publications, experimental methods, or engineering safety assessments.

Tools and technologies

  • Next.js 16 and React 19: Used to develop the web application, structure its pages, and implement interactive components, dashboards, and research exploration features.
  • TypeScript 5.9: Used for strongly typed code, improving code reliability, maintainability, and development efficiency.
  • Tailwind CSS 4, PostCSS, and Custom CSS: Used to create responsive layouts, visual styling, interactive charts, animations, and the platform's space-inspired interface.
  • ESLint 9: Used for code linting, identifying potential issues, and maintaining consistent coding practices.
  • CSV Files and Local Project Data: Used to store, organize, process, and retrieve NASA investigation records, experimental measurements, and other research-related datasets.
  • Python and Matplotlib: Used to provide optional, downloadable Python scripts that allow users to reproduce selected data visualizations. Running these scripts requires Matplotlib to be installed in the user's Python environment.
  • Node.js and npm: Used for project execution, package management, dependency installation, and development workflow management.
  • Visual Studio Code (VS Code): Used as the primary development environment for writing and editing source code, generating and organizing project files, and managing different file formats, including CSV datasets.
  • OpenAI Codex CLI: Used as an AI-assisted development tool to accelerate boilerplate code generation and support parts of the implementation process.
  • Groq Platform: Used to integrate API-based AI capabilities into the Super Intelligence dashboard, enabling context-aware responses to research queries using the platform's available information and user-provided context.
  • Netlify: Used for website deployment and hosting, making INFLAMIOTIC accessible online.



AI disclosure:

AI has been used only in generating code as well as descriptive text which has been further reviewed by the team, in order to align with the general theme of the competition.

All resources and documents gathered, as well as external intergrations such as API keys integrated with the website done to the website are done by the team itself.

What makes it creative

INFLAMIOTIC combines a space-themed research interface with interactive ways to inspect combustion data. It pairs investigation summaries with source-linked tables and visual comparisons, and uses an evidence-linked simulator to make experimental conditions more approachable. The design aims to feel immersive while keeping the research itself central.

The project also contains simulations as well as an AI-powered dashboard that answers query based on the context of the website as well as user-customizable context that can be given to better cater to the needs of the research.


The project also contains various sections and aspects of the datasets which have been analyzed in both a textual and visual manner keeping in mind the accessibility to the maximum number of people.

The project also contains downloadable CSV files as well as downloadable bar charts
The platform also features an interactive material-selection dashboard, where users can adjust various parameters through customizable sliders to explore material suitability for specific applications. By evaluating different conditions and material properties, the dashboard provides comparative insights to support informed material selection.

Additionally, INFLAMIOTIC examines historical fire incidents, connecting their underlying causes and contributing conditions to relevant NASA combustion research. It explores how insights from these studies could have helped mitigate similar fire hazards, highlighting the potential role of scientific research in improving fire-safety strategies for future space missions.


Factors the team considered

The team considered scientific accuracy, readability, accessibility, and the difference between measured results and interpretation.

Hence this project is a project, that anybody can read, interact and use easily.

Charts use the available source measurements; curated investigation scores are presented as approximate research-prioritization aids. Files without numeric flame results are treated as indexes or summaries, rather than being plotted as experimental outcomes.

Scores given in certain sections are not NASA-represented scores but rather AI-powered rankings of materials on various factors to just a simple score that shows from 1 to 10 in order to understand the best materials for the job.

The responsive layout, contrast, and reduced-motion preferences were also considered.
